references.text: The elders of the city have legal authority in cases involving killing and bloodshed, which shows their role as judges in serious matters.
The appointment of judges and officials in all cities demonstrates the established legal system of which the elders and judges in Deuteronomy 21:2 are a part.
Witnesses and investigation are necessary in murder cases, reflecting the need to measure the distance to the cities to determine responsibility.
Cities of refuge and their role in cases of unintentional killing are related to the procedure for handling unsolved murders.
The elders of the nearest city shall perform the cleansing ritual, which shows why measuring the distance is important.
